sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In 2016, the Swedish Tourist Association announced a new service called the Swedish Number.
sentences.zh: 2016年，瑞典旅游局宣布推出一项名为“瑞典号码”的新服务。

sentences.en: If you dial the telephone number, plus 46-771-793-336, you will be connected with a random Swede.
sentences.zh: 如果你拨打这个电话号码加46-771-793-336，你将会接通一个随机的瑞典人。

sentences.en: You will soon be connected to a random Swede somewhere in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 你很快就会接通瑞典某地的随机瑞典人。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Hello, this is Olle.
sentences.zh: 喂，我是奥勒。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to Sweden.
sentences.zh: 喂，欢迎来到瑞典。

sentences.en: Oh, hi.
sentences.zh: 噢，嗨。

sentences.en: Is this a random Swedish person?
sentences.zh: 这是随机的瑞典人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a Swedish person.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个瑞典人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Cold calling the Swedes is Will Coley.
sentences.zh: 冷拨瑞典电话的是威尔·科利。

sentences.en: I'm a reporter and I have one question for you.
sentences.zh: 我是一名记者，我有一个问题想问你。

sentences.en: What do you think of when I tell you the date 3rd of September, 1967?
sentences.zh: 当我告诉你1967年9月3日这个日期时，你想到了什么？

sentences.en: 1967, September 3rd.
Could maybe be.
sentences.zh: 可能是吧。

sentences.en: The left to right.
sentences.zh: 从左到右。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the one we changed to right and perfect.
sentences.zh: 对，那是我们改成右侧的，很完美。

sentences.en: We called about a dozen Swedes and for the most part, if they are alive and in country for any part of the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我们大约给十几个瑞典人打了电话，在很大程度上，如果他们在20世纪60年代的任何时候活着且在国内。

sentences.en: The date, September 3rd, 1967, was a hugely important and heralded day.
sentences.zh: 1967年9月3日这个日子，是一个极其重要且备受瞩目的日子。

sentences.en: Dagen H.
sentences.zh: H日。

sentences.en: Dagen H.
sentences.zh: H日。

sentences.en: H-day.
sentences.zh: H日。

sentences.en: Yeah, H-day, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，H日，对。

sentences.en: Short for Högge Trafikomlagningen or something like that, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这是右侧交通转换的简写之类的。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Högge Trafikomlagningen.
sentences.zh: 右侧交通转换。

sentences.en: Meaning the right-hand traffic diversion.
sentences.zh: 意思是右侧交通改道。

sentences.en: H-day was the day that 7.8 million Swedes switched the side of the road they drive on, from the left side to the right.
sentences.zh: H日是780万瑞典人将他们驾驶的道路一侧从左侧切换到右侧的日子。

sentences.en: It would be the most massive overhaul in driving infrastructure that any country had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 这将是任何国家见过的最大规模的驾驶基础设施改造。

sentences.en: Historically, if you're riding a horse, generally you want to keep to the left so that you can use your right hand to greet passers-by.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，如果你骑着马，通常你希望靠左行驶，以便你可以用右手向路人打招呼。

sentences.en: Or, you know, whack them with a sword.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，用剑砍他们。

sentences.en: But with the advent of the horse-drawn carriage, there were some conditions in which it made sense to stick to the right, and customs could vary by country.
sentences.zh: 但随着马车的出现，在某些情况下，靠右行驶是有道理的，习俗也可能因国家而异。

sentences.en: And as cars became more common, they followed the same laws that were established for horse-drawn traffic.
sentences.zh: 随着汽车变得越来越普遍，它们遵循了为马车交通制定的相同法律。

sentences.en: Up until 1967, Sweden drove on the left side of the road.
sentences.zh: 直到1967年，瑞典一直靠道路左侧行驶。

sentences.en: Which set it apart from its neighboring countries, Finland, Norway, and Denmark, all of which drove on the right.
sentences.zh: 这使它有别于其邻国芬兰、挪威和丹麦，这些国家都靠右行驶。

sentences.en: And this presented probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这就带来了问题。

sentences.en: The biggest problem was the accidents.
sentences.zh: 最大的问题是事故。

sentences.en: With Swedish drivers abroad, and the visitors in Sweden, who also had difficulties with the change from right-hand driving to left-hand driving.
sentences.zh: 由于瑞典司机在国外，以及在瑞典的游客，他们在从靠右驾驶转换为靠左驾驶时也遇到了困难。

sentences.en: And these accidents increased continuously.
sentences.zh: 这些事故不断增加。

sentences.en: This is psychologist Anders Englund.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学家安德斯·恩格伦。

sentences.en: When he says left-hand driving, he means driving on the left-hand side of the road.
sentences.zh: 当他说左侧驾驶时，他的意思是沿着道路的左侧驾驶。

sentences.en: When Anders started working with the Swedish government in the 1960s,
sentences.zh: 当安德斯在20世纪60年代开始与瑞典政府合作时，

sentences.en: they were tired of seeing Swedes getting into car accidents abroad and having tourists and truck drivers from other countries getting into car accidents in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 他们厌倦了看到瑞典人在国外发生车祸，以及来自其他国家的游客和卡车司机在瑞典发生车祸。

sentences.en: There was also some motor vehicles that were adapted to right-hand driving.
sentences.zh: 还有一些适应右舵驾驶的机动车辆。

sentences.en: Swedish car companies made vehicles that were meant to be driven on the right, so they could be exported more easily.
sentences.zh: 瑞典汽车公司制造了旨在靠右行驶的车辆，以便它们可以更容易地出口。

sentences.en: But these cars also found their way onto roads in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 但这些汽车也出现在瑞典的道路上。

sentences.en: And that was a problem.
sentences.zh: 那是个问题。

sentences.en: Namely, having your steering wheel on the outside edge of the road.
sentences.zh: 也就是，把方向盘放在道路的外侧边缘。

sentences.en: Overtaking or pausing, as you say, in your country, you don't see the oncoming cars.
sentences.zh: 正如你们国家所说，超车或停车时，你看不到迎面驶来的汽车。

sentences.en: It was a big mess.
sentences.zh: 这是一团糟。

sentences.en: The Swedish government thought it could get a lot better if they just switched what side of the road they drove on, if they could drive on the right like most of Europe.
sentences.zh: 瑞典政府认为，如果他们只是切换驾驶道路的一侧，如果他们能像欧洲大部分地区一样靠右行驶，情况就会好很多。

sentences.en: Legislative action to switch driving the side had been attempted before, a few times actually.
sentences.zh: 此前曾尝试过改变驾驶侧的立法行动，实际上有过几次。

sentences.en: But it always failed.
sentences.zh: 但总是失败。

sentences.en: And then, in the early 1960s, the Swedish government thought that this could be the time.
sentences.zh: 然后，在20世纪60年代初，瑞典政府认为这可能是时候了。

sentences.en: They put it to a public vote, asking the Swedish populace to decide.
sentences.zh: 他们将其交付公众投票，让瑞典民众来决定。

sentences.en: The answer from the people was a resounding no.
sentences.zh: 人民的回答是一个响亮的否定。

sentences.en: 83% of the people in Sweden voted for keeping left-hand driving.
sentences.zh: 瑞典83%的人投票赞成保持靠左驾驶。

sentences.en: So the government just went ahead and did it anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以政府还是直接照做了。

sentences.en: Sweden likes to be looked upon as a democratic country.
sentences.zh: 瑞典喜欢被视为一个民主国家。

sentences.en: And despite that, the government decided that we must change this.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，政府还是决定我们必须改变这一点。

sentences.en: Anders England served as part of the team that would help make that change.
sentences.zh: 安德斯·恩格兰是帮助实现这一变革的团队成员之一。

sentences.en: I was secretary in the scientific working group.
sentences.zh: 我是科学工作组的秘书。

sentences.en: As secretary, Anders supervised three teams, one assessing what methods they should deploy for an educational campaign, one trying to forecast what problems they might encounter,
sentences.zh: 作为秘书，安德斯监督了三个团队，一个评估他们应该为教育运动部署什么方法，一个试图预测他们可能遇到什么问题，

sentences.en: and a third one for mass media.
sentences.zh: 第三个负责大众媒体。

sentences.en: One of Anders' jobs was helping to come up with informational materials for the switch, like a pamphlet that would explain what would be different, what to watch out for,
sentences.zh: 安德斯的工作之一是帮助为转换想出宣传材料，比如一本小册子，解释会有什么不同，要注意什么，

sentences.en: and what rules to follow.
sentences.zh: 以及要遵守什么规则。

sentences.en: And just take a second to think about what kind of a job this is.
sentences.zh: 花一秒钟想想这是个什么样的工作。

sentences.en: If you've ever been in a car driving on the opposite side of what you're used to, everything feels wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经坐在车里，在与你习惯的方向相反的道路上行驶，一切都感觉不对劲。

sentences.en: So you need to teach people to identify what is actually correct, even though it feels wrong, and what's actually just wrong, wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要教人们识别什么是真正正确的，即使它感觉不对，以及什么是真正错误的、错误的。

sentences.en: The pamphlet Anders and his team worked on shows where your car goes when you make a right turn or a left turn, how to pass, what pedestrians should be aware of.
sentences.zh: 安德斯和他的团队制作的小册子展示了你转右弯或左弯时汽车去哪里，如何超车，行人应该注意什么。

sentences.en: How they should move.
sentences.zh: 他们应该如何移动。

sentences.en: How they should drive.
sentences.zh: 他们应该如何驾驶。

sentences.en: The two most important things that the pamphlet did was, one, to familiarize Sweden with a new traffic sign.
sentences.zh: 这本小册子做的两件最重要的事情是，第一，让瑞典熟悉一个新的交通标志。

sentences.en: The six-formed sign with a leaning H in the middle.
sentences.zh: 中间带有倾斜H的六边形标志。

sentences.en: A hexagon sign with an H in it.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个H的六边形标志。

sentences.en: H for höger or right.
sentences.zh: H代表höger或右。

sentences.en: These signs would be visible on the roads after the switch.
sentences.zh: 转换后，这些标志将在道路上清晰可见。

sentences.en: And there were also little stickers with an H you could put on the inside of your windshield to remind yourself while you're driving.
sentences.zh: 还有带有H的小贴纸，你可以贴在挡风玻璃内侧，以便在开车时提醒自己。

sentences.en: In fact, you might still spot an H-sticker inside some of the older cars in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你可能仍然会在瑞典的一些老车里面发现H贴纸。

sentences.en: The second super important part of the public education campaign was the date of the switch.
sentences.zh: 公众教育运动的第二个超级重要的部分是转换的日期。

sentences.en: September 3rd, 1967.
Dog and hoe.
sentences.zh: 狗狗和锄头。

sentences.en: H-day.
sentences.zh: H日。

sentences.en: The pamphlet was a good start in getting people ready for H-day, but soon the government realized they needed to bring out the big guns.
sentences.zh: 这本小册子是让人们为H日做好准备的一个良好的开端，但很快政府意识到他们需要拿出杀手锏。

sentences.en: They wanted to unleash their nation's most effective weapon for penetrating people's hearts and minds.
sentences.zh: 他们想释放他们国家最有效的武器，以深入人心。

sentences.en: Pop music.
sentences.zh: 流行音乐。

sentences.en: Sweden's television station had put out a competition to come up with the best song to teach people about H-day.
sentences.zh: 瑞典电视台发起了一场竞赛，旨在创作出最好的歌曲来向人们介绍H日。

sentences.en: The winner, the tell stars with Haldig till Höger Svensson.
sentences.zh: 获胜者是The Telstars演唱的《Haldig till Höger Svensson》。

sentences.en: Translation, keep to the right Svensson.
sentences.zh: 翻译，坚持向右斯文森。

sentences.en: Svensson being a stereotypically common Swedish last name like Smith or Jones.
sentences.zh: 斯文森是一个刻板印象中常见的瑞典姓氏，就像史密斯或琼斯。

sentences.en: There's also a bit of wordplay here.
sentences.zh: 这里也有点双关语的意思。

sentences.en: In Swedish, keeping to the right is shorthand for being faithful to your spouse.
sentences.zh: 在瑞典语中，靠右是忠于配偶的简写。

sentences.en: Going left means having an affair.
sentences.zh: 向左走意味着有外遇。

sentences.en: The government had spent four years getting the country ready.
sentences.zh: 政府花了四年时间让国家做好准备。

sentences.en: The official H-day pamphlet had gone out to every Swede.
sentences.zh: 官方的H日小册子已经发给每个瑞典人。

sentences.en: The Svensson song had lodged itself in people's brains.
sentences.zh: 斯文森之歌已经深深印在人们的脑海中。

sentences.en: PSAs had saturated the airwaves.
sentences.zh: 公益广告已经充斥了广播电台。

sentences.en: I samband med övergången till högertrafik går man över från gul till vit färg för markeringar på vägbanan.
sentences.zh: 在向右侧交通过渡的同时，路面标线也由黄色改为了白色。

sentences.en: September had arrived.
sentences.zh: 九月已经到来。

sentences.en: The evening of the second became the morning of the third.
sentences.zh: 二号的晚上变成了三号的早晨。

sentences.en: Everyone knew the drill.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这一套流程。

sentences.en: H-day was here.
sentences.zh: H日到了。

sentences.en: All non-essential traffic was banned from the roads from late night to early morning.
sentences.zh: 从深夜到清晨，所有非必要的交通都被禁止上路。

sentences.en: Most cars were kept off the road.
sentences.zh: 大多数汽车都不准上路。

sentences.en: The only people on the roadways were construction crews,
sentences.zh: 道路上仅有施工人员，

sentences.en: taxi drivers who were given the okay from the government.
sentences.zh: 获得政府批准的出租车司机。

sentences.en: And a hand-picked few, like this guy.
sentences.zh: 以及少数精挑细选的人，比如这家伙。

sentences.en: It was great fun.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: There were very few cars out in Stockholm.
sentences.zh: 斯德哥尔摩街头极少有汽车。

sentences.en: And I, like one of the very few, got the permission to drive at night when it was forbidden.
sentences.zh: 而我，就像极少数人一样，获得了在禁止通行的夜晚开车的许可。

sentences.en: This is Bo Holmström.
sentences.zh: 这是博·霍尔姆斯特伦。

sentences.en: Well, I'm Bo Holmström.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是博·霍尔姆斯特伦。

sentences.en: I'm a Swedish journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我是一名瑞典记者。

sentences.en: I've been working since 1960 in the television as a television reporter.
sentences.zh: 我自1960年以来一直在电视台工作，担任电视记者。

sentences.en: In 1967, I was working on the switch to right-hand drive traffic and doing a lot of stories about it.
sentences.zh: 1967年，我致力于右侧驾驶交通的转换，并做了很多关于它的报道。

sentences.en: Bo is actually a pretty famous broadcast journalist, kind of like a Swedish Tom Brokaw.
sentences.zh: 博实际上是一个相当著名的广播记者，有点像瑞典的汤姆·布罗考。

sentences.en: At the time, this was the big story.
sentences.zh: 当时，这是一个重大新闻。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: We were on the air almost all night, and the day after two, transmitting from different points in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎整晚都在播音，第二天也有两天，从瑞典的不同地点进行传输。

sentences.en: Bo Holmström.
sentences.zh: 博·霍尔姆斯特伦。

sentences.en: Riksdagshuset är ju egentligen en plats där man är van vid att hålla på dygnet om nästan vid senande banter.
sentences.zh: 瑞典议会大厦其实是一个人们习惯了几乎夜以继日地进行辩论的地方。

sentences.en: Work crews were out putting up the hexagonal H signs, the ones reminding you to drive on the right.
sentences.zh: 工作人员正在外出张贴六角形的H标志，这些标志提醒你要靠右行驶。

sentences.en: Plus, they had to flip around and move pretty much every street sign in the country.
sentences.zh: 另外，他们不得不翻转并移动国内几乎每一个路标。

sentences.en: What I saw was changing of signs, turning them the other way, and changing of signs at bus stops.
sentences.zh: 我看到的是更换标志，把它们转向另一边，以及更换公交车站的标志。

sentences.en: It was such a great feeling to be biking around, 10 years old, and there was no traffic.
sentences.zh: 10岁的时候骑着自行车到处转，而且没有交通，这种感觉太棒了。

sentences.en: A few of the random Swedes that we reached on the phone were also there on each day.
sentences.zh: 我们在电话中联系到的一些随机瑞典人当时也在每一天。

sentences.en: And then, of course, they have a song that was going repeatedly on the radio.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，他们有一首在收音机里反复播放的歌。

sentences.en: I can't record it, but try to rewrite Svensson or something.
sentences.zh: 我无法录制它，但试着重写斯文森或类似的东西。

sentences.en: Roundabouts were reconfigured for people to go counterclockwise instead of clockwise.
sentences.zh: 环岛被重新配置，人们逆时针行驶而不是顺时针。

sentences.en: Freeway off-ramps became on-ramps.
sentences.zh: 高速公路下匝道变成了上匝道。

sentences.en: Temporary bus stops were set up in the middle of the street to accommodate buses that now had doors on the wrong side.
sentences.zh: 临时公交车站建在街道中央，以容纳现在门开错边的公交车。

sentences.en: At 4.50 a.m., a horn blared across Stockholm, and a loudspeaker announced,
sentences.zh: 凌晨4点50分，斯德哥尔摩响起了一声喇叭，扬声器宣布，

sentences.en: Now is the time to change over.
sentences.zh: 现在是转换的时候了。

sentences.en: And then, under the direction of thousands of traffic cops dispatched around the country,
sentences.zh: 然后，在部署在全国各地的数千名交通警察的指挥下，

sentences.en: all of the cars in Sweden made their way to the right.
sentences.zh: 瑞典的所有汽车都驶向右侧。

sentences.en: For the most part, the H-Day transition team had accounted for everything.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，H日过渡团队已经考虑到了所有事情。

sentences.en: But it was disorienting, and not everyone was a happy camper.
sentences.zh: 但这让人感到迷失方向，并不是每个人都高高兴兴。

sentences.en: Some people said they got loSt.
sentences.zh: 有些人说他们迷路了。

sentences.en: They were in their own city.
sentences.zh: 他们在自己的城市。

sentences.en: They had been driving there for years.
sentences.zh: 他们在那儿开了很多年车。

sentences.en: They were used to take a one-way street, for example, and there was still one way, but the other way.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们习惯走单行道，那里仍然是单行道，但方向相反。

sentences.en: So they couldn't go where they wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以他们无法去他们想去的地方。

sentences.en: I remember one old lady or middle-aged lady sitting in the passenger seat in one car we stopped,
sentences.zh: 我记得在我们拦下的一辆车里，有一个老太太或中年妇女坐在副驾驶座上，

sentences.en: and she was mad, mad as hell, saying,
sentences.zh: 她很生气，气极败坏地说道，

sentences.en: We didn't want this.
sentences.zh: 我们不想要这个。

sentences.en: We voted against it.
sentences.zh: 我们当时投了反对票。

sentences.en: Everybody was against going over.
sentences.zh: 所有人都反对转换方向。

sentences.en: Damn politicians.
sentences.zh: 该死的政客。

sentences.en: They didn't start a war.
sentences.zh: 他们虽然没挑起战争，

sentences.en: But they're going to get thousands of people killed in the traffic instead.
sentences.zh: 但却要在交通上害死成千上万的人。

sentences.en: But here's the really amazing thing about H-Day and the shift as a whole.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于H日以及整个交通靠左/靠右制的转变，最惊人的地方在于：

sentences.en: The total number of traffic-related deaths on H-Day was zero.
sentences.zh: H日当天与交通相关的死亡人数为零。

sentences.en: In fact, the total number of accidents went down for a while.
sentences.zh: 事实上，事故总数在一段时间内还有所下降。

sentences.en: There were a lot of people thinking that this should be a catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 当时很多人以为这会是一场灾难。

sentences.en: There should be thousands of dead people in the traffic.
sentences.zh: 交通上应该会死成千上万人才对。

sentences.en: It didn't.
sentences.zh: 但并没有发生。

sentences.en: Likely because everyone was so freaked out about driving on what felt like the wrong side of the road
sentences.zh: 这很可能是因为大家对在感觉像是逆行的路面上开车感到极其恐慌，

sentences.en: that for a while, everyone drove really slowly and carefully.
sentences.zh: 所以在一段时间里，所有人都开得格外缓慢和小心。

sentences.en: A year after Sweden switched sides of the road,
sentences.zh: 瑞典更改行车方向一年后，

sentences.en: Iceland also switched to driving on the right to be more like the rest of Europe,
sentences.zh: 冰岛也为了更贴近欧洲其他地区而改成了靠右行驶，

sentences.en: the United Kingdom and Ireland notwithstanding.
sentences.zh: 英国和爱尔兰则除外。

sentences.en: In the 1970s, former British colonies, including Ghana and Nigeria,
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代，包括加纳和尼日利亚在内的前英国殖民地，

sentences.en: switched from left to right to be more like their neighbors in West Africa and the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 从靠左行驶改为了靠右行驶，以便与西非的其他邻国及世界其他地方保持一致。

sentences.en: Today, the vast majority of the world drives on the right.
sentences.zh: 如今，世界上绝大多数国家都靠右行驶。

sentences.en: And in places that do drive on the left, like in the U.K.,
sentences.zh: 而在那些确实靠左行驶的地方，比如英国，

sentences.en: movements occasionally spring up trying to get the country to switch to the right.
sentences.zh: 偶尔也会出现一些试图让国家改回靠右行驶的运动。

sentences.en: But there is one notable exception, where a country went left.
sentences.zh: 但有一个引人注目的例外，那就是有一个国家改成了靠左行驶。

sentences.en: Office of the Prime Minister of Samoa, how may I help you?
sentences.zh: 萨摩亚总理办公室，请问有什么可以帮您？

sentences.en: Samoa.
sentences.zh: 萨摩亚。

sentences.en: Oh, hi, this is Will Coley calling from New York.
sentences.zh: 哦，你好，我是来自纽约的威尔·科利。

sentences.en: Hello, Mr. Coley.
sentences.zh: 你好，科利先生。

sentences.en: Samoa is an island republic in the South Pacific,
sentences.zh: 萨摩亚是南太平洋的一个岛国共和国，

sentences.en: not to be confused with American Samoa, which is just east of Samoa.
sentences.zh: 不要与位于萨摩亚正东方的美属萨摩亚混淆。

sentences.en: In 2009, they did the opposite of Sweden and nearly every other country who made the switch.
sentences.zh: 2009年，他们做出了与瑞典以及几乎所有其他做出改变的国家相反的举动。

sentences.en: They went from driving on the right to driving on the left.
sentences.zh: 他们从靠右行驶改为了靠左行驶。

sentences.en: Will Coley called up the guy responsible for the change.
sentences.zh: 威尔·科利打电话给负责这项变革的人。

sentences.en: Okay, well, hold on for a minute.
sentences.zh: 好的，请稍等一会儿。

sentences.en: I'll transfer the call.
sentences.zh: 我来转接电话。

sentences.en: Okay, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Yes, this is the actual whole music for the office of...
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是……办公室实际的整段背景音乐。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Hi, Prime Minister?
sentences.zh: 您好，是总理先生吗？

sentences.en: Yes, Prime Minister of Samoa.
sentences.zh: 是的，萨摩亚总理。

sentences.en: Do you have to say no, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 你得说不、不、不、不、不、不。

sentences.en: For Prime Minister Malele Moy, switching to the left offered one major obvious benefit,
sentences.zh: 对总理马勒莱·莫伊来说，改成靠左行驶带来了一个显而易见的主要好处，

sentences.en: aligning Samoa more closely with the biggest nearby economies,
sentences.zh: 那就是让萨摩亚与周边最大的几个经济体联系得更加紧密，

sentences.en: Australia, New Zealand, and Japan.
sentences.zh: 也就是澳大利亚、新西兰和日本。

sentences.en: All of which drive on the left.
sentences.zh: 这些国家全部都是靠左行驶。

sentences.en: Well, it's something that we have been thinking about for a long time,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我们考虑了很久的事情，

sentences.en: mainly because we needed to import cheaper cars.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为我们需要进口更便宜的汽车。

sentences.en: Samoa wanted to import cheap used cars from nearby Japan.
sentences.zh: 萨摩亚想要从邻近的日本进口廉价的二手车。

sentences.en: Japan has the cheapest second-hand car market in the world.
sentences.zh: 日本拥有世界上最便宜的二手车市场。

sentences.en: But cars in Japan are made to be driven on the left,
sentences.zh: 但日本的汽车是为靠左行驶而制造的，

sentences.en: so Samoa decided to make the switch to left-side driving.
sentences.zh: 所以萨摩亚决定转为靠左行驶。

sentences.en: It's pure common sense.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是常识。

sentences.en: By all accounts, the day of the switch, September 7th, 2009, was really smooth.
sentences.zh: 据各方报道，2009年9月7日转换行车方向的那天非常顺利。

sentences.en: It probably helped that there were only a couple of major roads to modify.
sentences.zh: 这可能要归功于当时只有几条主要道路需要改造。

sentences.en: It began with a radio announcement from Prime Minister Malayla Maui.
sentences.zh: 它始于总理马勒莱·莫伊的一则广播讲话。

sentences.en: Today, we will launch a great event that will be most helpful to our livelihood,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将启动一项对我们生计极有帮助的伟大活动，

sentences.en: and that is to drive on the right-hand side of the road.
sentences.zh: 那就是在道路右侧行驶。

sentences.en: And the switch was magnificent.
sentences.zh: 这次转变非常棒。

sentences.en: It was perfect.
sentences.zh: 简直完美。

sentences.en: That was great, but you said right-hand.
sentences.zh: 这很好，但你刚才说的是右侧。

sentences.en: I think you meant left-hand, right?
sentences.zh: 我想你的意思是左侧，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, sorry, sorry.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对不起，对不起。

sentences.en: Stick to the right, Svensson.
sentences.zh: 靠右行驶，斯文森。

sentences.en: Prime Minister Malayla Maui, stick to the left.
sentences.zh: 总理马勒莱·莫伊，请靠左行驶。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Will Coley and Sam Greenspan,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由威尔·科利和萨姆·格林斯潘制作，

sentences.en: with Katie Mingle, Sharif Youssef, Delaney Hall,
sentences.zh: 合作制作人有凯蒂·明格、谢里夫·优素福、德莱尼·霍尔、

sentences.en: Kirk Kohlstedt, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 柯克·科尔施泰特、艾弗里·特拉弗勒曼以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Peter Kincaid, author of Rules of the Road.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢《道路规则》一书的作者彼得·金凯德。

sentences.en: Also thanks to Diana Kincaid, Yuan Niklasen, Gustav Algren, Ambassador Fattori Elisaia,
sentences.zh: 还要感谢黛安娜·金凯德、袁·尼克拉森、古斯塔夫·阿尔格伦、大使法托里·埃利萨亚、

sentences.en: Boris Lindquist, Kate Montague, Rowena Fatuava Vavatao, and the Swedish Radio Archives.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·林德奎斯特、凯特·蒙塔古、罗威娜·法图阿瓦·瓦瓦陶以及瑞典广播电台档案馆。

sentences.en: And thanks to our random Swedes, Kenneth Johnson, Lucas Nielsen, Hans Bjorkman,
sentences.zh: 感谢我们的随机瑞典人，肯尼斯·约翰逊、卢卡斯·尼尔森、汉斯·比约克曼、

sentences.en: Mona Nortezavi, and Yula Grunas.
sentences.zh: 莫娜·诺特扎维和尤拉·格鲁纳斯。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 电台的一个项目，

sentences.en: and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 节目制作于 ArcSign 的办公室，

sentences.en: an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 这是一家位于美丽的奥克兰市中心（加利福尼亚州）的建筑与室内设计公司。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并喜欢这个节目。

sentences.en: Follow us all on Twitter and Instagram,
sentences.zh: 请在 Twitter 和 Instagram 上关注我们所有人，

sentences.en: but the best way to explore the 99% invisible activity that shapes the design of our world
sentences.zh: 但探索塑造我们世界设计的 99% 隐形现象的最佳方式，

sentences.en: is to click around the hundreds of stories,
sentences.zh: 是在 99pi.org 上点击浏览成百上千个故事，

sentences.en: now both audio stories and print stories,
sentences.zh: 现在这些故事既有音频版也有文字版，

sentences.en: on 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 尽在 99pi.org。
